original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colimit-kappa}
Let $X$ be a scheme. There exists a cardinal $\kappa$ such that
every quasi-coherent module $\mathcal{F}$ is the directed colimit
of its quasi-coherent $\kappa$-generated submodules.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 3554 asserts existence of some cardinal κ generating the relevant directed-colimit property for all quasi-coherent modules on arbitrary X. The reconstruction chooses an INFINITE cardinal, which is equivalent because any witness κ can be enlarged to max(κ,ℵ0), and κ-generation is monotone. No unrelated size bound is introduced.
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. There exists an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ such that
every quasi-coherent module $\mathcal{F}$ is the directed colimit
of its quasi-coherent $\kappa$-generated submodules.
conclusions:
There exists an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ such that
every quasi-coherent module $\mathcal{F}$ is the directed colimit
of its quasi-coherent $\kappa$-generated submodules.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-coherator}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is a Grothendieck
abelian category. Consequently, $\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has enough injectives and all limits.
\item The inclusion functor
$\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
has a right adjoint\footnote{This functor is sometimes called
the {\it coherator}.}
$$
Q : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \longrightarrow \QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
such that for every quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction mapping
$Q(\mathcal{F}) \to \mathcal{F}$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
stage_b_review_note: Pinned proposition 3633 says QCoh(O_X) is a Grothendieck abelian category, hence has enough injectives and all limits, and that inclusion into Mod(O_X) has a right adjoint Q which restricts to identity on QCoh through its counit. The draft retains both independent clauses, adjunction direction, and counit.
